chapter: Hite tours, postwar L.A. and the Central Avenue scene
title: Singers and dancers at the Apex and Sebastian's
summary: Strut Mitchell, May Ellix, Baby Mack, Eddie Anderson, and others.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Who were some of the other artists? You mentioned that there were some people that worked at the
Apex or the Alabam who were -- I think we were talking about the Apex -- who were known mostly only on the West Coast.

Oh, in those old days, there were singers like a fellow they called Strut Mitchell. He was a singer and a dancer. There were lady singers and dancers like, for instance, there was a girl by the name of May Ellix (PHONETIC) out of Chicago, very beautiful, attractive woman, that sang and danced. There was Sue Hoy (PHONETIC) and there was Martha Richie (PHONETIC) and Baby Mack. Baby Mack was Les Height's wife. Baby Mack Height. There was a toe dancer, one of the first black toe dancers I ever saw in my life by the name of Mary Richards. Rochester " Eddie Anderson started there and later went out to Sebastian's Cotton Club. He had a partner by the name of Johnny Taylor. There was the two of them, Johnny Taylor and Eddie Anderson. That was before Jack Benny picked him up. That's where Jack Benny got Eddie Anderson, Rochester, from Sebastian's Cotton Club, when we were working out there.
